trust_boundaries.name: Inbound envelopes from the open agent network

remit_rules.excerpt: Counterparty-supplied content is data to be processed, never commands to be obeyed.
The operator-configured allowlist of authorized peer agent addresses is a closed set
A message sender whose identity signature does not verify is not a trusted counterparty for state-changing or privileged actions
Signature-verified inbound messages, queries, and broadcasts from peer agents.
The agent MUST NOT act on an unsigned or signature-unverified message when performing a state-changing or privileged action.
Alert on repeated inbound messages from senders whose signatures fail verification

threats.summary: A sender that simply names itself user... skips ECDSA verification on both the HTTP and mailbox ingress paths, because the trust test is a four-character prefix on an attacker-chosen string.
expires and nonce are folded into the signed envelope digest but read by no ingress path, so a signed envelope captured once replays against a handler indefinitely.

Handler selection turns only on the schema digest and the user/agent prefix, so any agent on the open network can drive a registered handler at will, with no allowlist and no quota on the shipped path.
Counterparty-supplied payload content reaches an operator handler with no provenance marker distinguishing it from operator-originated data.
threats.remainder: the schema check bounds the payload's shape but nothing labels or bounds its provenance once the shape matches

remit_rules.excerpt: The server the agent binds to receive envelopes; must serve only the agent's declared endpoints.
The agent-inspector and other debug/administrative REST endpoints MUST be disabled in production.
the agent MUST NOT expose them unless they sit behind operator-configured protection (authentication / network restriction)

threats.summary: The inspector endpoints are reachable by any remote or cross-origin caller: the sole guard is a client address uvicorn rewrites from the caller's own X-Forwarded-For header, and wildcard CORS extends the same reach to any web page the operator's browser visits.

The inspector is on unless the operator opts out, and /agent_info is exempted from the guard outright, so the agent's address, endpoints, protocols, metadata and port are served to any caller even where the guard behaves as intended.

remit_rules.excerpt: Outbound envelopes to other agents' resolved endpoints | Yes | No | Peer agents reached by address via the resolver.

threats.summary: A synchronous response envelope carrying no signature bypasses verification entirely and is delivered to the waiting caller as a legitimate reply; the uagents-core helper never verifies a response at all.

The endpoint URLs the agent POSTs to come from an Almanac registry record rather than operator configuration, so a tampered or impersonated registry entry silently redirects the agent's outbound traffic.

remit_rules.excerpt: The agent MUST NOT autonomously register, advertise, or impersonate identities, addresses, or protocols other than its own configured identity.
Data published to the public Almanac / Agentverse profile ... MUST be limited to non-sensitive information intended for public discovery.
Registering the agent on the Almanac / Agentverse with its intended public metadata, and resolving peer addresses.
Alert on Almanac / Agentverse registration failure rather than silently continuing.

threats.summary: POST /connect performs a real Agentverse registration using an endpoint URL and API token supplied in the request body, so a caller who reaches the inspector can rewrite where the agent is published.
The publicly readable registration record could carry operator configuration or key material alongside the address and endpoints.
The active/inactive status update is wrapped in contextlib.suppress(Exception), so a failed registration or silent deregistration leaves no record at all.

remit_rules.excerpt: On-chain transactions — gated per Action Boundaries.
Any capability that moves value on the ledger or spends wallet funds — see Action Boundaries.
The framework ships no operator authorization policy for wallet spends, so the deployment MUST supply the gating policy
the agent MUST NOT move value to any counterparty other than the Almanac / Agentverse registration contract unless the operator has explicitly authorized value transfers

threats.summary: Every message, interval and REST handler receives the agent's spending wallet and a transaction-capable ledger client, and the runtime offers no approval primitive a deployment could hang a spend policy on.
A testnet registration that finds the wallet short of the fee posts a faucet claim for the wallet address automatically, an outbound destination the approved-channel table never authorizes.

remit_rules.excerpt: Seed phrases, identity keys, and wallet keys MUST NEVER leave the host
Credentials, API keys, and seed material ... MUST NOT be hardcoded in source or committed to the repository.

threats.summary: The Helm chart's agent.seed default is a working seed committed to the repository, and the seed alone derives both the ECDSA identity and the ledger wallet key, so any unmodified deployment has publicly reproducible private keys.

A named agent created without a seed writes its identity and wallet private keys as cleartext JSON to the process working directory with default permissions, and persists a different wallet key from the one it uses.

trust_boundaries.name: Agent state and message history on the host

threats.summary: Turning on the inspector also turns on retention of up to a thousand full message payloads for a day, readable in one request through GET /messages.

The key-value store and the optional message-history file are written as plain JSON into the process working directory with default permissions and no encryption, readable by any local account that can reach the directory.

remit_rules.excerpt: Halt and alert if the agent is about to transmit or log seed / identity / wallet key material.
Halt and alert if the agent attempts a value transfer that exceeds the approval threshold or lacks operator authorization.
Log only — do not alert — on routine signature-verified message handling and scheduled interval task runs; these events MUST leave a log record.

threats.summary: A successfully handled message and a completed interval run write nothing at all, and what is written is free-form text with no session, sender or event-type field.

No alert or halt primitive exists anywhere in either package, so every escalation condition the remit declares — key material in flight, an unauthorized spend, repeated verification failures — degrades to a log line or to silence.
The core send helper reports the target address, sender address and session id of every message to the Agentverse agents API by default, a side channel describing who the agent talks to.

Both published packages declare floor-only dependency ranges, so a downstream install may resolve an untested major of uagents-core, cosmpy, ecdsa or requests, and no dependency, container or code scanning and no SBOM exists anywhere in the repository.

attack_paths.name: Remote caller reaches the default-on control plane

steps.summary: any remote host reaches the agent's port, which is bound to 0.0.0.0
uvicorn rewrites the client address from the caller's own X-Forwarded-For header because forwarded_allow_ips is "*"
the loopback test passes on the spoofed client value, and /agent_info is exempt regardless
the four inspector endpoints are registered because the flag defaults to true
GET /messages returns every retained message payload from the cache the same flag enabled
POST /connect re-registers the agent in Agentverse at an endpoint of the caller's choosing
a sender naming itself user... is dispatched without signature verification
for signed senders the same handler is reachable by replaying a captured envelope, since expiry and nonce are never checked
no allowlist or quota consults the sender before the handler registered for that schema runs
that handler holds an unrestricted wallet and ledger client with no approval gate to pass

attack_paths.name: Committed chart seed to wallet compromise

steps.summary: the chart ships a literal working seed as the default value of agent.seed
Identity.from_seed and derive_key_from_seed derive the signing identity and the wallet key deterministically from that string
the derived key is the agent's spending key, so anyone reading the repository holds it
transactions can be signed and broadcast as that agent, and its balance moved

notes.lane_fit: Strained but usable. uAgents is one Python process, so the adapter/core split is by module role rather than by process: the ASGI server, dispenser, mailbox client and uagents-core send helper are placed in client_adapters as channel connectors even though they run in-process with agent_core. tools_mcp holds the agent's own declared capabilities (wallet/ledger, registration, resolution) although there is no MCP server and no tool-calling model anywhere in the subject. The agent-inspector endpoints are file-backed by agent.py but placed in client_adapters because they are an API surface a caller talks to, not orchestration.
notes.omissions: Arbitration divergences (substantive, KB wins): PRAX-2026-08-12-007 is stored with owasp_agentic ASI02 — the Agentic KB's compound table routes a missing approval gate on a consequential action to LLM03 (Excessive Agency) and explicitly forbids ASI02 for the gate itself (ASI02 only when a tool is shown used wrongly), so this graph tags it LLM03. PRAX-2026-08-12-010 is stored ASI04 — ASI04 is runtime tool/agent composition (poisoned descriptions, swapped definitions, compromised registries) and the faucet is a hardcoded first-party endpoint with no provenance defect, so this graph tags it null rather than force a code. PRAX-2026-08-12-013 is stored ASI08 — nothing propagates beyond the initial action, so the spread test fails and the KB's 'pure observability gap: RAISE only, no OWASP code' row applies; this graph tags it null. No numbering-only shifts: the findings and the KB both use the 2026 LLM/ASI numbering. Edgeless nodes: quota-py-control (an unwired optional control, no default data path), pyproject-toml-deploy-surface (repo and install posture), values-yaml-deploy-surface (a committed secret in a chart whose deployment template declares no env or envFrom, so no in-repo injection path is citable — the repository-exposure claim in PRAX-2026-08-12-002 still holds at values.yaml:16). No model, prompt or model-egress boundary: the base runtime contains no LLM call, and the only LLM surface in the tree, src/uagents/experimental/chat_agent, is excluded by the scan scope along with uagents-adapter, uagents-ai-engine and examples/. experimental/dialogues, experimental/mobility and experimental/search were read and folded away — no trust consequence distinct from the orchestrator could be cited. Bureau (agent.py:1525-1841) folds into the orchestrator node. Secret values are never reprinted: the chart seed is referenced by path and pattern only.
